text: Every model and test built so far only gets checked when someone remembers to run it by hand. This lesson wires that check into GitHub itself, on every single pull request.

Three things matter: each pull request gets its own disposable Snowflake schema; build and test run as two separate checks; and the check is marked required, so GitHub disables the merge button until it passes.
The workflow checks out the branch, installs dbt, then builds and tests against a schema named for that exact pull request -- so two PRs can never collide.
We proved it works by pushing a PR that deliberately breaks a test. GitHub blocked the merge immediately. Revert the break, and the same PR goes green.
A broken model can no longer reach the schemas Finance, Marketing, and Product query. Next: making the pipeline that feeds those schemas run itself, every night, with Airflow.
